questions.q: What does the AI Readiness Score measure?
options: How ready an account's data is for AI workloads, combining demand coverage and semantic view readiness into a 0-100 score
How much compute a warehouse has consumed this month
How many roles have been granted access to a given table
How fast a Cortex Agent responds to a query
questions.explain: The AI Readiness Score scores assets on freshness, completeness, governance maturity, and model compatibility, combining demand coverage and semantic view readiness into one composite number.

options: What percentage of real analytical query traffic lands on tables marked consumption-ready, versus raw or half-modeled ones
How many terabytes of data a table stores
How many users have logged into Snowsight this week
How many Cortex Agents exist in the account
questions.explain: Demand coverage looks at actual query traffic hitting the account and checks what share of it lands on consumption-ready (CR) tables.

questions.q: What are the two parts of semantic view readiness?
options: Coverage (do consumption-ready tables have a semantic view at all) and Quality (how complete that view is)
Speed and Cost
Rows and Columns
Freshness and Encryption
questions.explain: Semantic view readiness splits into Coverage — whether a CR table has a semantic view — and Quality — how complete it is, with keys, relationships, metrics, descriptions, and verified queries.

questions.q: What is Horizon Context built on?
options: Semantic Views — the same object Cortex Analyst queries
Row access policies exclusively
Virtual warehouses
Snowpipe ingestion pipelines
questions.explain: Horizon Context turns metadata into governed business meaning using Semantic Views, the same construct behind Cortex Analyst, so every AI/BI consumer shares one trusted definition.

questions.q: In this lesson's real example, why does the opportunities list rank ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_METRICS above other low-coverage schemas?
options: It has the highest read volume (276,043 reads) with zero semantic-view coverage, making it the highest-value place to build one first
It is the oldest table in the account
It has the most columns of any table
It already has full semantic view coverage
questions.explain: The opportunities list ranks by actual query volume against uncovered consumption-ready tables, so the highest-read, zero-coverage schema is the top priority.
